findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is null/empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array. handleNewBooking.ts sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` (not `[]`) when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and several webhook handlers set `[]`. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) and safely fell back to Cal Video in that case. Booking a Google Meet event type for a user without a destination calendar will now crash event creation instead of falling back to the daily video integration.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback is dead code, causing undefined calendarId for legacy bookings
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — in the else branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `find` compares `cal.externalId === undefined/null` and can never match; the fallback always evaluates to `undefined`. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. For any booking whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId` (all bookings created before this PR, and new ones where the destination fell back to "primary"), `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`, so rescheduling/updating those bookings fails against the Google API.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback silently deletes from "primary", orphaning events on real destination calendars
findings.body: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — since `externalCalendarId` is falsy in the fallback branch, the `find` predicate can never match and the result is always `undefined`. The code then falls back to `defaultCalendarId` ("primary"). For bookings created before this PR whose references have no `externalCalendarId`, cancelling now attempts deletion from the user's primary calendar; Google returns 404, which the error handler treats as success (`if (err.code === 404) return resolve()`), so the actual event on the configured destination calendar is silently left behind. The previous code deleted from `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`.

findings.title: Post-insert patch uses possibly-undefined selectedCalendar
findings.body: After `calendar.events.insert` succeeds, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (which adds the hangout link to the description) passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, but `selectedCalendar` is the result of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and is `undefined` whenever no destination calendar matches the credential — the insert call itself guards this with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the patch does not. When the event was created on "primary" because no destination matched, the patch is issued with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the video link never gets added to the event description for those bookings.

findings.title: Organizer attendee email taken from first destination calendar even when creating on another host's calendar
findings.body: In `createEvent`, the organizer attendee's email is set to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` (the first entry of `destinationCalendar`), while the event is actually created on `selectedCalendar`, the calendar whose `credentialId` matches the credential being used. For a collective event with multiple hosts, when creating the event on the second host's Google calendar, the organizer is still recorded with the first host's calendar address. The event on the non-primary host's calendar gets a wrong/mismatched organizer, which can misattribute the event and misroute organizer responses. The email should correspond to the destination calendar selected for that credential (i.e. `selectedCalendar`).

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always targets the first destination calendar regardless of credential
findings.body: `createEvent` derives the events URL from `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId` (`/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events`). With the new multi-destination support, EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents invokes this service once per host's credential, but the service always writes to the first host's calendar externalId while authenticating with whichever host's credential was passed. For a collective event where a non-first host uses Office365, the Graph API call targets another user's calendar id with the wrong token, failing (or writing to the wrong calendar). The service needs to select the destination calendar matching the active credential, like the Google service does with `credentialId`.

findings.title: CalDAV base service filters by first destination calendar, silently creating no event for other hosts
findings.body: In `BaseCalendarService.createEvent`, calendars are filtered by `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` — the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. When EventManager creates events for a collective booking with multiple CalDAV hosts, the service instance for host B authenticates as host B but filters the calendar list against host A's `externalId`; no calendar matches, `responses` is empty, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and the method returns a successful `NewCalendarEventType` without creating any event. Host B silently gets no calendar event while the booking reports success. The filter must use the destination calendar that corresponds to the credential being used, not `destinationCalendar[0]`.

findings.title: Lark createEvent uses first destination calendar's externalId with the wrong credential
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;` — with multiple destination calendars (the new collective-event behavior), the Lark service always uses the first host's calendar id no matter which host's credential is instantiated. When EventManager iterates destinations and creates an event for a non-first host via their Lark credential, the request `/calendars/${calendarId}/events/create_event` targets the first host's calendar with the second host's access token, which either fails with a permission error or writes to the wrong calendar. Like GoogleCalendarService, the calendar should be resolved by matching `credentialId`.

findings.title: Condition for setting team slug inverted relative to previous behavior
findings.body: The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts the logic: previously the organization's team row got `slug` only when team billing was NOT enabled; now it gets `slug` only when billing IS enabled. This is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (destination calendars) and is not explained in the description. On deployments where `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, newly created organizations will no longer have a team slug, breaking organization URLs that previously worked. If the inversion is intentional it needs its own PR/justification; otherwise this is a regression.

findings.title: Team destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, which is exactly the value assigned a few lines above when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. For a collective event where the organizer/event type has no destination calendar but team member hosts do have one, those hosts' calendars are silently discarded and they get no calendar event — the core scenario this PR is meant to fix. The push should happen unconditionally, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

findings.title: updateEvent result lacks credentialId/externalId, so updateLocation creates references without credential linkage
findings.body: `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns only `{appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, originalEvent, calError, calWarnings}` — it never sets `credentialId` or `externalId`, even though `EventResult` now declares them and `EventManager.updateLocation` (editLocation.handler.ts) builds `referencesToCreate` from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. Every booking reference created after a location edit will therefore have `credentialId: undefined` and `externalCalendarId: undefined`, degrading all later updates/cancellations to the legacy "iterate all calendar credentials" path and losing the per-host credential targeting this PR adds. `updateEvent` should return `credentialId: credential.id` and the external calendar id like `createEvent` does.

findings.title: destinationCalendar webhook payload shape changed from object to array — breaking change for consumers
findings.body: Changing `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` changes the JSON payload sent to all BOOKING_CREATED / BOOKING_REJECTED / BOOKING_CANCELLED / BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook subscribers (the whole `evt` is sent via `sendPayload`). Existing integrations that read `payload.destinationCalendar.integration` or `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will now get `undefined` because the value is an array. The PR is labeled "non-breaking change" and no migration/communication for webhook consumers is included; the e2e expectations in webhook.e2e.ts confirm the payload shape changed. This should be documented as a breaking change or the payload should keep backwards compatibility.

findings.title: No tests added for the multi-destination-calendar behavior
findings.body: The PR explicitly states "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works", while it rewrites the calendar-event creation/update/deletion flow across EventManager, CalendarManager, three calendar services, cancellation, and payment webhooks. There is no unit test covering: a collective booking creating one event per host's destination calendar, cancellation deleting all hosts' events via the new per-reference credentialId handling, or the legacy single-destination fallback for pre-existing bookings. Given the regressions visible in the fallback paths (e.g. undefined calendarId in Google updateEvent/deleteEvent), regression tests for existing bookings without `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId` references are particularly important before merging.
